Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Latin word

significō

significō, significāre, significāvī, significātum

verb, first conjugation

indicate, show, make known; mean, signify (of a word or a sign)

In this lexicon

  • indicate

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Fam. 7.18.1: significābant enim tē istam mīlitiam jam firmō animō ferre; Traupman 247, 332: significāre, indicate

  • mean

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Tusc. 1.88: carēre igitur hoc significat: egēre eō quod habēre velīs; Traupman 30

Examples

  • significābant enim tē istam mīlitiam jam firmō animō ferre et esse fortem virum et cōnstantem

    for they showed that you are now bearing your military service with a steady mind, and are a brave and steadfast manCic. Fam. 7.18.1

    In the entry for indicate

  • Parātae lacrimae īnsidiās, nōn flētum indicant.

    Tears at the ready indicate a trick, not grief.Publil. Sent. P 61

    In the entry for indicate

  • Quid volt sibi, Syre, haec ōrātiō?

    What does this talk mean, Syrus?Ter. Heaut. 615

    In the entry for mean

  • carēre igitur hoc significat: egēre eō quod habēre velīs

    So “to lack” means this: to be without what you would like to have.Cic. Tusc. 1.88

    In the entry for mean

  • plēraque sunt vocābula quibus vulgō ūtimur, neque tamen liquidō scīmus quid ea propriē atque vērē significent

    There are many words we use every day without knowing clearly what they properly and truly mean.Gell. 16.5.1

    In the entry for mean

  • Quid hoc verbum significat?

    What does this word mean?composed
